research_rooms.about: The Research Library is organized into ten rooms. Each study has one home room and may also appear in one or two others. Everything here is official research.

thesis.headline: We're living through a revolution. America's institutional systems are being reconstructed from the root — not by tearing the old order down, but procedurally, from inside it, through its own laws, agencies, money and machinery.
thesis.kicker: And we get front-row seats to watch it being built, live.

packages.question: How does the Board convert the Eccles-1951 OIG diagnosis into a durable operating constitution for major initiatives outside its core monetary, regulatory and supervisory expertise?
packages.bluf: The Federal Reserve OIG's September 29 Eccles-1951 report creates a broader institutional test: when the Board undertakes construction, planned IT modernization or another major initiative outside its core expertise, it should operate as a nonexpert owner that imports specialized leadership, independent challenge, fixed baselines, open-book cost evidence, materiality-based escalation and senior oversight independent of day-to-day management. The diagnosis, seven recommendations and Chairman Warsh's GSA, audit, GMP, metrics, remedy and permanent-standards directions are established. The operative GSA instrument, auditor engagement, validated awards, signed ceiling, recovery, agency-wide framework, first reuse and durable closure are not yet established.

packages.title: Federal Reserve, Clearing and Treasury
packages.question: Who may access, clear, settle or control public money and collateral across the Federal Reserve, Treasury and private clearing utilities?
packages.bluf: The September 29 Federal Reserve OIG evaluation closes the criminal and administrative-misconduct allegations within its scope but finds a serious management failure: the Board did not effectively execute the Eccles-1951 construction-manager-at-risk contract, had no agreed project-level guaranteed maximum price after more than $2,000,000,000 was awarded, underused its owner representative, allowed 84 limited-scope packages to set price without an overall ceiling and repeatedly reported the project as on track against rebased benchmarks. Construction rose from a $921,000,000 February 2020 budget to a $2,018,000,000 December 2024 budget; four MEP awards alone rose from a $206,000,000 estimate to $694,000,000. Inflation and site/design conditions mattered, but the OIG found the criticized marble, fountains, garden terrace and related features were not material cost drivers. Chairman Warsh concurred and directed GSA project leadership, an independent cost audit, GMP negotiations, fixed metrics and contract remedies; these are directed corrective actions, not yet a ceiling, validated final cost or recovered dollar. The September 29 American Express feedback dispute exposes a resolution-planning classification seam: the Federal Reserve and FDIC identified significant uncertainty in the feasibility of a one-buyer sale across an FDIC bank receivership and two Chapter 11 estates, yet found no deficiency or shortcoming. Regulation QQ permits additional feedback, but its shortcoming definition uses closely related feasibility language; Gould's dissent therefore targets the opacity and structural leverage of unclassified feedback, not the statutory existence of living wills. The September 20 legal-status and records-routing matrix establishes that the Federal Reserve has no single public/private status: the answer varies by actor, function, statute, record custody and remedy. The Board is a federal agency; the FOMC is an APA/FOIA agency; each Reserve Bank is a separate federally chartered corporation whose agency, instrumentality, employer, person and liability status changes by legal regime. Records likewise route by function and control rather than physical host: Bank-held material can be an FOMC record, a current-rule Board record, or a Bank record subject to the Banks' voluntary transparency policy and other lawful access routes. The companion appointment, removal and succession chain maps five distinct personnel constitutions from Governors and Reserve Bank directors through FOMC officers, SOMA management, the Inspector General and Bank general auditors; it also restores the August whole-government FRFS/National IT committee constitution to the direct package's discovery routes. The Wave 4 reconciliation confirms that the prior committee map was already substantial and classifies its bodies by legal effect: statutory Board/FOMC/Bank-board decisions, Board advisory and delegated routes, PSPAC policy advice, COP/Payments Committee/AFRC/ITOC enterprise governance, CPE/FRFS management, Richmond/National IT hosting and independent assurance. It distinguishes PCSC, PSPAC and the presidents' Payments Committee and preserves the unpublished charters, votes, materiality tests and application RACI as proof gaps. Wave 5 separates inspection and recommendation from approval, conditioning, direction, injunction, removal and institutional suspension. It finds extensive but nonuniversal audit, preserves GAO's monetary-policy exclusions and Dodd-Frank exceptions, defines the clean 2025 outside-audit limits, and locates actual stopping power in Board/Bank-board/FOMC/Treasury/court/congressional instruments rather than in the audit label itself. Wave 6 finds no unitary Federal Reserve crisis commander: insured-bank resolution, daylight and Discount Window credit, §13(3), FOMC/SOMA operations, payment and cyber incidents, Buddy Reserve Bank continuity, §248(h) intervention, cash logistics and Treasury fiscal-agent recovery have distinct legal principals, operators, books, finality and exit rules. It separates participant buddy banks from inter-Reserve-Bank continuity and service restoration from transaction reconciliation. Wave 7 reconstructs the twelve corporations' foundation: the Federal Reserve Act is the congressional charter; filing a district organization certificate created the body corporate; the Comptroller's separate certificate authorized business; and bylaws govern internally beneath federal law. It inventories all twelve current-posted bylaws and twenty-four Branches, distinguishes statutory member stock from ordinary equity, and identifies the direct St. Louis certificate plus exact missing constitutive, election, seal and title records. The September 20 congressional-oversight map shows why the Federal Reserve is not legally a fourth constitutional branch while preserving the real accountability critique: Congress created the System, controls its statutes and institutional design, confirms Governors through the Senate, mandates testimony, reports, audits and disclosures, and can amend or repeal the architecture; yet self-funding, long protected terms, nonconfirmed Reserve Bank presidents, GAO exclusions, OIG jurisdictional seams and monetary-policy exceptions deliberately insulate immediate policy operations. The vault-canonical factual spine and current Workbench extensions show how the Fed can retain the dollar unit and crisis backstop while private clearing moves into the middle and the twelve Reserve Banks specialize inside a common operating machine. The whole-site evidence supports contested functional unbundling and reduced daily visibility, not established castration, abolition, merger, private capture or removal. The September 20 dollar-issuance constitution shows that the Federal Reserve's role is a congressional statutory operating arrangement, not a private agreement or transfer of U.S. sovereignty. Congress defines the unit and legal-tender system; Treasury issues coins, retains capped United States-note authority and prints Federal Reserve notes; the Board orders and authorizes those notes; Reserve Banks issue notes into circulation and maintain central-bank balances; and private deposits and stablecoins remain legally distinct claims. Congress can restructure or replace that architecture by ordinary federal law, while executive orders, regulations and operator contracts cannot rewrite the statute. The companion congressional change history proves this is not merely theoretical: from 1927 corporate succession and the 1930s governance and gold rewrites through the 1977 objectives, 1980 monetary-and-payment reach, 2008 interest on reserves, 2010 emergency-credit limits and 2025–26 digital-money boundaries, Congress has repeatedly expanded, constrained and reallocated Fed powers. It also separates legislative dissolution from violation-based franchise forfeiture and the public dollar unit from Federal Reserve notes and private redeemable dollar claims. The Oklahoma City hearing audit shows that Congress was hardening the digital-public-money boundary, but the June 12 exchange did not establish illegal CBDC issuance or a §11(h) forfeiture case: no current Fed policymaker admitted ongoing work, the enacted §16A prohibition postdated the hearing, the House text predated it, and the public post-order projects reviewed do not establish creation of a U.S. central-bank liability. The September 20 payment-system mandate map shows that fostering safety and efficiency is a major Federal Reserve function but not a unitary third mandate parallel to Federal Reserve Act §2A. Congress supplied tool-specific powers that the Board, twelve Reserve Banks, private operators and co-regulators exercise through operation, access, intraday liquidity, rules, supervision, oversight and coordination; safety, efficiency and accessibility must therefore be tested at each lifecycle layer. The September 16 interest-rate constitution adds the missing rate-setting process: the FOMC target, administered tools, transaction benchmarks, auctions, traded yields and customer contracts are separate objects, and private, tax, insider, public-credit and credit-union below-market lanes have different authority and consequence. Its overnight-money companion follows the actual reserve-account, Fedwire, unsecured-credit, rollover and ON RRP mechanics beneath the policy rate and distinguishes Federal Reserve balances from commercial nostro/vostro claims. The September 18 DTCC whole-site refresh supports a regulated modular-conversion reading: DTCC is rebuilding legal submission, machine-readable reporting, operating hours, fund distribution, asset records and settlement interfaces while preserving incumbent membership, account, risk, correction and finality controls. AnnounceDirect, CMU CSV conversion, Fund/SERV tokenization access, 24x5 clearing, DTC tokenization and settlement modernization remain distinct objects with distinct proof gates rather than one common launch.

The transparency extension shows that stablecoins can expose a public transfer record while reserves, beneficial ownership, direct redemption, complete cost, legal finality and remedy remain institutionally governed. The accounting extension now has a full-thesis front door: legal and economic meaning, signed events, purpose-specific official records, versioned rules, judgment objects, continuous subledgers, reporting, control, assurance and remedy remain separate layers across sixteen accounting functions, eight business cycles, multiple legitimate views, eight clocks and an evidence ladder. Oracle–Swift, smart contracts, blockchain recordkeeping and continuous-assurance tools are placed as bounded mechanisms and early evidence gates rather than treated as the transition itself. A targeted September 3 refresh records OCC preliminary conditional approval for proposed World Liberty Trust Company, N.A.; the bank still cannot commence business before final approval, and its planned USD1 transfer from BitGo remains future-state. A bounded September 15 state-credit-union audit finds a real Florida/Wyoming public-deposit seam and an explicit possible Wyoming stable-token connection, but no enacted state-owned credit union, 0–3 percent lending program or demonstrated credit-union role in either digital-money chain. The bounded September 23 SEC 24-hour-trading return finds a scheduled 23x5 expansion rather than live 24x7 operation: execution, market data and clearing availability are lengthening on different clocks while issuer disclosure, corporate actions, supervision, cash and finality remain separate boundaries. The September 24 Fed/CFTC work adds a page-complete 452-page reading of the proposed Board-supervised stablecoin issuer constitution and bank-subsidiary application gateway plus current CFTC staff guidance for tokenized eligible assets and on-chain records; the Fed architecture is projected through its own seven-layer, twelve-gate Hub rather than treated as one flat rule overlay. The September 30 OUSD launch return identifies Bridge Building Inc. as issuer and redemption obligor, Open Standard as the partner-economics and prospective governance company, and Mastercard as a founding investor and advertised access route after completing BVNK; four-chain supply and the issuer reserve dashboard are live, while a Mastercard customer receipt, independent monthly attestation and published consortium constitution remain open.

packages.title: Banks and Credit Unions — Federal and Four-State Legal Architecture
packages.question: What legally distinguishes banks from credit unions, which rules come from the federal government, and how do Florida, Wyoming, New York and Texas use their remaining charter, public-deposit, tax, supervision and digital-asset authority?
packages.bluf: The United States has overlapping bank and credit-union dual-charter systems rather than one national regime. Charter, ownership, regulator, insurer, account eligibility, public-funds permission, digital authority and operating state must be recorded separately. Florida and Texas maintain active state-bank and state-credit-union charters and admit credit unions to public deposits; New York maintains both charters but its ordinary local-deposit law still excludes credit unions; Wyoming charters banks and SPDIs but has no current state-credit-union law, so its credit unions are federally chartered even when state law admits them to public funds.

packages.title: International Monetary Transition
packages.question: Which reserve, settlement, invoicing, FX and stablecoin changes constitute diversification, pricing or actual monetary substitution?
packages.bluf: Reserve diversification, regional settlement and trade invoicing remain separate from actual monetary substitution. Bessent's April 2026 IIF scorecard adds the incumbent strategy and a three-way legitimacy contest. The IMF symmetry audit finds candid surveillance of systemic members but operationalized, finance-linked adjustment for borrowers. The July 31 Japan–Korea cases and saved August Japanese confirmation distinguish national intervention and dealer prices from a separate stablecoin quote; the disclosed aggregate does not resolve every trade date, allocation or U.S. funding leg. Korea's observed token price transmission is not net capital flow; Japan's limited production rails are not shown to have supported intervention. The September 1 Asheville G20 Chair's Statement adds agreed work on digital assets and payment modernization, but China expressly objected to four paragraphs and the statement itself is not implementation or monetary substitution. Masu's September 10 BOJ speech supplied an individual hawkish-normalization signal. The September 28 July-meeting minutes and the September 18 decision close the first rate-decision clock: the Board raised the overnight target and complementary deposit rate to 1.25 percent effective September 24. The minutes show bank lending remained strong, major/regional and shinkin outcomes diverged, and no new prudential rule was made; JGB-stock-runoff, bank-level transmission, market-stability and digital-rail clocks remain separate. The Japan Monetary Constitution build uses balance-sheet movement as its empirical spine. Layer 0 finds that the 2021–2026 JGB–HKD link synchronized BOJ-recorded JGB title with HKMA central-bank money without creating a new claim or merging finality; the September 11 retirement is established, while utilization, rationale and successor remain unknown. Layer 1 finds embedded BOJ independence inside a braided Diet–Cabinet–MOF–BOJ–FSA authority structure: the BOJ can operate a JGB auction without buying the debt, execute MOF intervention without deciding it, and settle government funds without authorizing expenditure. Layer 2 finds a multi-book transition: the BOJ's audited fiscal-2025 balance sheet contracted by ¥66.742 trillion; reserve remuneration more than doubled and the Treasury payment fell; sovereign debt and interest expense rose on separate government clocks; and current MOF/FEFSA intervention is material while the latest monthly operation's direction remains undisclosed. Layer 3 finds asymmetric private transmission: bank core margins improved, but shinkin net income fell and regional banks realized ¥1.136 trillion of bond losses; floating borrowers repriced on staged clocks; GPIF absorbed ¥14.753 trillion of domestic bonds while its bond sleeve lost 5.11 percent; and capital, stress tests and delinquency data still show an orderly system. Layer 4 finds private JGB risk-bearing inside public finality: MOF shortened issuance toward investor capacity, recent benchmark auctions remained covered, and repo and JSCC intermediate funding and default risk, while BOJ-NET retains title and yen settlement and the BOJ retains collateral, scarcity-lending and contingent-purchase authority. Layer 5 finds singleness without sameness: cash, BOJ reserves, bank deposits, safeguarded provider balances, trust stablecoins and tokenized deposits share a denomination but not a debtor, ledger, asset or failure path. JPYSC is live but closed-loop and tiny; DCJPY remains an issuing-bank deposit; both BOJ CBDC tracks remain pre-production. The concrete digital-money balance-sheet change is the 2026 capacity to move up to half of a trust-stablecoin reserve from demand deposits into qualifying short sovereign securities or term deposits, adding valuation, liquidity and contribution clocks without giving tokenholders title to the reserve asset. Layer 6 finds many interfaces but few finality rooms: BOJ-NET supplies wholesale yen finality and JGB title; Zengin's large-value RTGS, small-value DNS and More Time clocks can put customer credit ahead of interbank finality; and its collateral and private mutualized loss rules keep liquidity distinct from loss. Zengin-Net's own 2026 diagnosis supports constitutional refactoring under infrastructure strain, but the conditional fiscal-2030 replacement and unresolved settlement asset do not establish crisis or a completed successor. Layer 7 finds mobility without monetary succession: Agorá's real-value tests, Swift's shared commitments, DCJPY, stablecoins, tokenized JGBs and the live Indonesia–Japan QR corridor move coordination and programmable control faster than they move debtor identity, final yen settlement or statutory title. Retail CBDC would create a direct public BOJ claim but remains unauthorized and simulated. The evidence supports constitutional refactoring through adapters, not current monetary replacement or an established legitimacy crisis. Layer 8 finds public continuity and layered loss: BOJ finality and Articles 33/37/38 liquidity sit at the public center, but BOJ credit is not intended to compensate solvency loss; DICJ insurance and resolution, TLAC, JSCC/Zengin waterfalls, fraud restitution and industry contributions allocate cost before legally gated fiscal support. The evidence supports concentrated classification power and bounded legitimacy pressure, while April 2026 capital, funding and stress results argue against a current systemic or legitimacy crisis. The final Japan proof follows six transaction and failure paths and rules for constitutional refactoring without monetary succession: plural risk-bearing inside public finality. It strongly supports concentrated finality and distributed balance-sheet burden, but not current monetary replacement, systemic crisis or an established legitimacy crisis; unequal protection and burden support only a bounded, falsifiable legitimacy-pressure inference. The governed six-lens visual makes the whole constitution, balance-sheet migration, JGB life cycle, payment-finality chain, digital adapters and failure/loss ladder inspectable while preserving the source owners and bounded states. The September 14 UK delta identifies collateral mobility as the near-term centre of the joint FCA–Bank wholesale-tokenisation program and opens a bounded FCA inquiry into eligible physical-gold ownership tokens, while preserving separate title, custody, collateral, settlement, finality, prudential, perimeter and failure clocks. The records support burden migration and constitutional refactoring, but not a present solvency or legitimacy-crisis claim.

packages.title: Insurance and Reinsurance
packages.question: Which sovereign and supervisory authorities define the insurance constitution, how do insurer balance sheets transmit monetary and capital-market policy, who transfers or retains risk, and which private or public balance sheet ultimately pays or recoups a covered loss?
packages.bluf: Big insurance is a distributed public-private balance-sheet constitution. Sovereign law and state legal-entity supervision form the base; NAIC coordination, lead-state tools, federal functional perimeters, IAIS standards and foreign supervisors add group and system windows without creating one insurance ministry. Across borders, global standards, domestic implementation, covered agreements, equivalence decisions, cooperation arrangements, group colleges, reserve-credit rules and resolution powers are distinct controls; none turns a group into one freely transferable balance sheet. At year-end 2025, FIO reported $9.902 trillion of life-sector assets and $3.223 trillion of property/casualty assets, making insurers major buyers of bonds, mortgages, structured assets and private credit. Monetary conditions, capital treatment, reinsurance and FHLBank liquidity can therefore transmit through insurer portfolios into borrower financing and market stress. Liquidity is a timed-cash problem distinct from solvency, while asset risk reaches statutory capital through a separate ratings, designation, accounting and RBC chain. Ownership adds another chain: proposed control, approval, closing, board governance, affiliate dealings, fees, dividends and support remain legally distinct, and owning insurer shares does not confer ownership of insurer assets. Pension risk transfer changes the obligor only through the chosen transaction, contract and distribution state; it also moves protection from the PBGC plan perimeter toward state-regulated annuity and guaranty frameworks. PMI, title, financial guaranty and surety can gate credit and execution before loss but do not erase the underlying duty. Compulsory financial responsibility starts above the policy by defining the activity, acceptable security, public proof and lapse consequence. Economic, statutory, investor and tax measurements remain distinct from capital and cash. Price-Anderson, commercial-space excess claims, FAA war-risk insurance and SAFETY Act protections use different private/public liability structures. Domestic insurer failure ordinarily passes through state receivership, bounded guaranty protection, assessments and estate recovery rather than ordinary chapter 7. Policy, claim, filing, custody and collateral records remain operational control objects: restoration is not reconciliation, and reconciliation is not completed remedy. Product-line and retail records are downstream evidence of this sovereign, supervisory, capital, ownership, risk-transfer, operational and public-loss machine.

packages.title: Economic Institution Legitimacy Crisis — 2025–2026
packages.question: Are economic institutions entering a legitimacy crisis as technological capability, private operating systems, executive coordination, standards and public-law structures change who can define money, access, records, rules, correction and failure?
packages.bluf: Waves 1–5 organize the legitimacy-crisis lens across 15 contrastive function cases and 119 dated events and feed a generated eleven-mode private thesis instrument. The opening Institutional Sovereignty Map asks who retains the control rights over purpose, admission, authorization, authoritative record, execution, settlement and delivery, loss and failure, and correction and remedy, while routing each function into existing factual owners rather than creating a new truth store. The September 24 Braided Thesis defines the parent frame as 1776 2.0—a procedural rebellion attempting to found a new operating order from inside the old one—and compares eight thesis objects at different altitudes across eight shared strands, the original seven arcs, seven genuine tensions, a combined rival and eight return gates without merging their factual owners. The September 24 Growth Architecture makes the positive-case theory inspectable across ten nodes from the human-scale dollar and live records through faster credit, programmable dollar rails, risk-bearing capital, physical buildout, operating capacity, growth as stability and the debt denominator; facts, inference and five-percent belief remain separate, and stablecoin scale is not treated as new risk capital raised. Dedicated Under the Hood and Fed Constellation rooms expose 19 technology objects, five System operating layers and the distinct contributions of all twelve Reserve Banks. The September 8 whole-site Reserve Bank recertification materially deepens the Constellation's operating face with Bank-hosted accounting, Treasury, payment, technology, procurement, data, HR, finance, cash, credit-risk, supervision and contingency functions. The separate September 22 research-and-sensing face adds each Bank's conference contribution and six recurring cross-System fields across AI, digital money, labor, infrastructure, data authority and resilience, while preserving attention as distinct from policy, ownership and operation. The September 30 movement-over-time face joins the July regional sweeps to those two owners and bounded late-September returns, exposing five cross-Bank trajectory fields while keeping speech, research, conference, survey, model, appointment, operation, authority and outcome separate. The September 30 innovation-controls face adds three technology corridors and seventeen control objects, following each through authority, operator, record owner, operating receipt, boundary and next gate; it identifies Systemwide internal AI and the FedNow data-and-risk layer as the fastest live movements without promoting proposal, access, standard, or research into production. The September 17 capital-markets specimen and September 18 mission-to-machine synthesis extend the thesis: institutions are restating retained public functions while execution is decomposed into selected portfolios, regulated claims, shared services, programmable records, private adapters, and new venue or settlement arrangements. The strongest recurring mechanism is that practical control can move faster than legal responsibility, authoritative records, supervision and remedy. Ordinary constitutional adaptation and successful incumbent absorption remain the strongest counter-reading, common architecture is not proof of common command, and no single function-level crisis state is treated as a proxy for the whole system. Katie has accepted the instrument as the project's living private orientation surface; it remains developing rather than a settled verdict.
